title: Component dimension is chart dimension at the generic point over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type: it is quasi-compact (every open covering of its point space has a finite subcover) and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume also that its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact). Give $|Y|$ its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Every irreducible component $C\subseteq |Y|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has a unique generic point $\eta_C$, meaning $\overline{\{\eta_C\}}=C$. For every representable etale map $a:U\to Y$ from a scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism] and every $u\in U$ with $a(u)=\eta_C$, one has
$$\dim_u|U|=\dim C\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}.$$
Here $C$ has its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology], $\dim C$ is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $\dim_u|U|$ is the infimum of the dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $u$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. No smoothness, reducedness, separation, geometric irreducibility or equidimensionality assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space (1); Tag 03K6, proposition-reasonable-sober; Tag 00OT, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field (1)=(2). Agent-formulated component-generic comparison for finite-type quasi-separated algebraic spaces, using the dimension comparison and the finite-type-over-a-field component dimension argument.

proof.text: Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $p:W\to Y$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The finite-type hypothesis on charts makes $W$ locally of finite type over $k$. Since $W$ is affine it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence finite type. Write $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$; [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] makes $A$ finitely generated over $k$, and [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes $|W|$ Noetherian. The map $|p|$ is continuous and surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus $|Y|$ is Noetherian: pull back any descending chain of closed subsets to $W$, let it stabilize there, and use surjectivity to infer stabilization of the original chain.

source.place: Tag 04Z8, lemma-image-Noetherian (1); affine atlas Tag 03H6, spaces-properties lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover; finite-type affine Noetherianity in algebra.tex.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components], write the finitely many components of $|Y|$ as $C=C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_r$. Sobriety from [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] gives the unique point $\eta$ with closure $C$. It lies in no other component: if $\eta\in C_i$, then $C=\overline{\{\eta\}}\subseteq C_i$, so maximality forces $C_i=C$. Consequently $O=|Y|\setminus\bigcup_{i>1}C_i$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta$ contained in $C$. All subsequent neighbourhoods will be taken inside this open.

source.place: Tag 03K6, proposition-reasonable-sober; topology.tex, finite-component decomposition and removal of all components other than C.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be the reduced closed subspace supported on $C$, supplied by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its pullback $T=Z\times_YW\to W$ is a closed immersion, with point image $p^{-1}(C)$, and $T\to Z$ is a surjective etale atlas by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By the affine quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for an ideal $I$. The images of a finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A$ generate $A/I$, so $T$ is finite type over $k$, and the chart criterion makes $Z$ locally of finite type. Also $|Z|=C$ is quasi-compact: it is closed in the quasi-compact space $|Y|$ (adjoin its open complement to a cover). Since $i$ is a monomorphism, its diagonal over $k$ is the base change of the diagonal of $Y$ along $Z\times_kZ\to Y\times_kY$. Quasi-compactness on scheme tests survives this base change by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Thus $Z$ is finite type and quasi-separated over $k$. The same diagonal argument proves that every open subspace of $Y$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 03K6, proof using a reduced closed support; spaces-properties.tex, reduced closed subspaces; affine closed immersion Tag 01QO; quasi-compact base change on scheme tests.

proof.text: Fix $w\in W$ above $\eta$. Let $N$ be any open neighbourhood of $w$ in $W$ contained in $p^{-1}(O)$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], its image is an open subspace $J\subseteq Y$ and $N\to J$ is surjective etale. The nonempty open $|J|\subseteq C$ is dense in the irreducible space $C$. Put $Z_J=Z\times_YJ$ and $T_J=T\times_ZZ_J$. The closed-support pullback clause of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] identifies $|Z_J|$ homeomorphically with $|J|$. The inverse image $T_J$ is an open dense subset of $T$: every nonempty open $B\subseteq T$ has nonempty open image in $Z$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], which meets the dense open $Z_J$, so $B\cap T_J\ne\varnothing$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison] to the finite-type scheme $T$ and its dense open $T_J$ to obtain $\dim T=\dim T_J$. The maps $T\to Z$, $T_J\to Z_J$ and $N\to J$ are surjective etale atlases, the middle one by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. All three targets are quasi-separated by step 3. Thus [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-atlas-dimension] and [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] give $\dim N=\dim|J|=\dim|Z_J|=\dim T_J=\dim T=\dim|Z|=\dim C$. This is a sequence of direct applications and a one-line density check. It never asserts that $N\to Y$ factors through the reduced subspace $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space (2), applied to the atlas of J; varieties.tex Tag 0A21, dense-open dimension argument on the component support.

proof.text: The neighbourhoods $N$ just considered form a neighbourhood basis at $w$: intersect any neighbourhood with the open set $p^{-1}(O)$, which contains $w$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], compute the local dimension inside this open subspace. Every open neighbourhood there has dimension $\dim C$ by step 4, so its infimum is $\dim C$ by [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Hence $\dim_wW=\dim C$ for every $w$ above $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0055, definition-Krull, local dimension as infimum over open neighbourhoods; restriction to an open neighbourhood.

proof.text: Now let $a:U\to Y$ and $u$ be as in the statement. The fibre product $V=U\times_YW$ is a scheme, and its projections to $U$ and $W$ are etale by representability and etale base change [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Surjectivity on pairs of field-valued point classes [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] supplies $v\in V$ mapping to $u$ and to some $w\in W$ above $\eta$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] to both scheme projections. It gives $\dim_uU=\dim_vV=\dim_wW=\dim C$. Neither $U$ nor $a$ needs to be quasi-compact or surjective.

source.place: Tag 04N4, lemma-dimension-at-point-local; comparison of any two etale scheme charts through their fibre product.

proof.text: The atlas $T\to Z$ of step 3 and [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-atlas-dimension] identify $\dim C=\dim|Z|=\dim T$. The scheme $T$ is finite type over $k$, so [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] makes this dimension finite. It is nonnegative since $C$ is nonempty and the atlas is surjective, so $T$ is nonempty and any point has a nonempty irreducible closure, a chain of length zero in the definition of Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This proves the asserted membership in $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ as well as the equality. If $Y$ is empty, it has no irreducible components and the statement is vacuous.
